newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate rises to 10.3 pct from 9.5.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate rises to 10.3 pct from 9.5.

text.p: Croatia's money market rate edged up 80 basis points to 10.3 on Friday on shorter supply as banks sought funds to stock up for the weekend.
Daily trade totalled 37.8 million kuna, of which 28.5 million were fresh borrowings. A surplus of 9.2 million kuna was left on the supply side.
Interbank rates ranged from 9.0 percent for call money borrowings and 15 percent for short term loans. State bank HBOR granted loans at call money rates of 12 percent.
There was no overnight trade on Thursday as all banks were liquid.
The central bank's kuna midrates for the weekend and Monday slightly eased to 5.4659 against the dollar and to 3.5618 versus the German mark. -- Laura Lui, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
